newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish election race narrows, opinion poll shows.
newsitem.headline: Irish election race narrows, opinion poll shows.

text.p: The popularity gap between the Irish coalition government and opposition is narrowing in the runup to elections expected within weeks, according to an opinion poll published on Thursday.

The MRBI survey published in the Irish Times showed that Prime Minister John Bruton's coalition was trailing opposition parties by six percentage points compared with a gap of 12 when the poll was taken in January.
The survey also showed that concern about crime has overtaken unemployment as the main election issue, with Ireland's rising drug problem the third main priority.

The election is not due until November. But political sources expect Bruton to call it early, possibly in May, to profit from Ireland's biggest tax reduction budget in January and a wave of job creation.

They said Bruton could announce a date when the cabinet met next Tuesday and logistical factors pointed to May 22 as a likely date. Bruton's government says it is imperative that Ireland be represented at a crucial EU meeting to change the European Union's treaty which is scheduled for mid-June.

Bruton's personal standing after two years in power is at an all-time high of 63 percent, up five points since January and that of Bertie Ahern, leader of the opposition Fianna Fail party, has fallen by one point.
Commentators said the poll was likely to encourage Bruton to announce an early election this month when parliament resumes.

His coalition, which groups the Labour party and Democratic Left, came to power in November 1994 when the government of Fianna' Fail's then Prime Minister, Albert Reynolds, collapsed in a row over legal appointments.
Fianna Fail, the biggest party in the country, has already hit the campaign trail with a series of hoardings promising that leader Bertie Ahern will put "people before politics".
His main election ally is expected to be the Progressive Democrats Party of Mary Harney, who is tipped to become foreign minister if Bruton's coalition is ousted.
The poll is taking place amid an unprecedented job creation boom thank to foreign investment, record economic growth and tax incentives by the government's IDA investment arm.
But the poll showed that crime has become the major preoccupation of the electorate, surpassing concern about he 11 per cent unemployment rate as top issue.
Petty crime, such as muggings and burglary, is rising steadily, according to police, but there has been a sharp and worrying increase in organised crime, especially drugs.
Heroin abuse has increased sharply. The street price has halved in the past three years and its use has spread from Dublin to other major towns and cities, police say.

The issue became the country's main concern last June after the country's top investigative journalist, Veronica Guerin, was shot dead at a traffic light by a suspected contract killer hired by a drugs baron she was investigating.

The MRBI poll showed that 43 per cent would prefer a Fianna Fail and Progressive Democrat coalition and 37 percent a Fine Gael/Labour grouping compared to 44 and 32 per cent respectively in a January poll.
